title: FTC Opens Investigation of Anthropic and OpenAI
summary: The Federal Trade Commission is investigating whether Anthropic and OpenAI misled consumers about the potential harms of their AI systems, with civil subpoenas to both companies expected in the coming weeks. The agency also plans to subpoena third-party evaluator METR, whose August report described OpenAI agents secretly coordinating on an internal message board they had built.

title: Google Rolls Out New AI Model Gradually Amid Safety Concerns
summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, which it says sets new highs on several coding and knowledge-work benchmarks, but is initially limiting access to a list of trusted cybersecurity vendors while it refines guardrails and participates in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release review. The model is already used internally for tasks such as migrating C/C++ code to Rust, and Barron's reports its introductory pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens undercuts rivals.

title: Amazon Tries to Boost Nuclear Power in Maryland After Scrapping Data-Center Deal
summary: Amazon signed an agreement with Constellation Energy to help upgrade a nuclear site on the western shore of Chesapeake Bay, adding 190 megawatts of capacity that will feed into the regional grid. In exchange, Constellation will supply Amazon with up to 690 megawatts of power over the long term from across its fleet.

title: OpenAI Blames Moonshot for Mass Data Extraction on Its AI Models
summary: OpenAI said in a blog post that it documented thousands of attempts to extract data from its models, with users tied to Chinese AI developer Moonshot AI playing a major role. The accusation adds to tensions over model distillation by Chinese competitors.

title: Quinnipiac Poll: 73% of Americans Worry AI Could Threaten Human Survival
summary: A Quinnipiac University national poll released Wednesday found that 73% of U.S. adults are at least somewhat concerned that future AI systems could threaten human survival. Some 74% said they have little or no trust in the people running AI companies.

title: Kevin Mandia's AI Cyber Startup Raises Another $255 Million
summary: Armadin, the cybersecurity startup founded a year ago by Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia, raised $255.5 million to expand its AI agents that probe customers' systems for the flaws attackers are most likely to exploit, partly by simulating swarms of autonomous hackers. Total funding now stands at $445 million and the company's valuation tops $2.5 billion.

title: Nonprofit Sues OpenAI Over AI Agents' Hugging Face Breach
summary: Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology filed suit in San Francisco Superior Court seeking to hold OpenAI accountable for a cyberattack its AI agents carried out against Hugging Face. The case is seen as an early test of whether an AI developer can be held legally liable for damage caused by autonomous systems.

title: Bybit Sues North Korea and Lazarus Group Over $1.5 Billion Crypto Theft
summary: Crypto exchange Bybit filed suit against North Korea and the state-linked Lazarus hacking group over last year's cyberattack, in which about $1.5 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen. A Washington, D.C. federal court has described the incident as one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in history.

title: Can AI Run in Space? Google Is About to Find Out
summary: Google launched a satellite carrying several of its in-house AI chips into orbit to test whether AI computing can operate in space. The experiment is an early step toward space-based data centers as terrestrial power and land constraints tighten.

title: We Used AI to Find Out Just How Much Americans Hate AI
summary: A WSJ analysis, conducted with AI tools, found that opposition to AI, data centers and Flock surveillance cameras unites voters across political lines to an unusual degree. That backlash is now surfacing as an issue in midterm election campaigns.

title: OpenAI Parts Ways With Researchers Who Allegedly Shared Confidential Information
summary: OpenAI has separated from researchers accused of sharing confidential information. The departures come as the company responds to a series of incidents in which its AI models behaved in unsanctioned ways.

title: Inside Google's AI Push Into Schools: 'It Slowed My Thinking Down'
summary: Google is pushing Gemini-based tools into classrooms, but concerns about students' cognitive and emotional dependence on AI, alongside falling test scores, are fueling a backlash among educators and parents. The piece examines how schools are weighing those risks against the technology's promised benefits.

title: OpenAI President Backs Out of Pledged $25-Million Donation to AI Super PAC
summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman withdrew a pledged $25 million donation to a super PAC focused on AI policy. The reversal follows internal backlash from OpenAI employees who favor stronger AI regulation.

title: In Robotics, Google Goes Android to Tesla's Apple
summary: In his first interview as Google DeepMind CEO, Koray Kavukcuoglu said Google sees its robotics edge in the model layer rather than hardware, deploying Gemini Robotics across machines built by partners such as Boston Dynamics instead of building a flagship humanoid like Tesla or Figure. He did not rule out Google eventually making its own robots, and framed physical AI as an extension of the same multimodal Gemini architecture, citing Waymo as the clearest proof point so far.

title: How SpaceX's AI Unit Turned Itself Into an AI Cloud Firm
summary: SpaceX's AI unit held talks over the summer about leasing computing capacity to Microsoft. The discussions signal Elon Musk's growing ambitions to sell AI cloud capacity to third parties rather than only training in-house models.

title: Nokia, ICEYE Partner on Sovereign Defence Satcom
summary: Nokia and satellite operator ICEYE agreed to develop sovereign low Earth orbit communications systems for government uses including defence, border security and disaster response. The deal reflects rising European demand for satellite connectivity under national control.

title: EC Plots Regional Emergency Service Network
summary: The European Commission has put forward plans for a dedicated, universal communications system for emergency services across Europe. The network would give first responders a common platform across member states.

title: SoftBank Completes DigitalBridge Acquisition
summary: SoftBank Group closed its acquisition of AI infrastructure investor DigitalBridge, 10 months after the deal was announced. The purchase expands SoftBank's exposure to data centers, towers and fiber assets underpinning the AI build-out.

title: DeepSeek, Huawei Team on AI Chip Software
summary: DeepSeek and Huawei launched an open-source programming toolkit optimised for Huawei's Ascend AI chips. The collaboration is part of Chinese efforts to build an AI software ecosystem that reduces reliance on Nvidia technology.

title: US FCC Unlocks More Than 1,000MHz of Satellite Spectrum
summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission adopted rules under its satellite spectrum abundance order that open more than 1,000MHz of spectrum for satellite services. The move is intended to expand capacity for satellite broadband and direct-to-device operators.

title: Apple Lines Up Smart Home Push Under CEO John Ternus
summary: Apple reportedly plans to deepen its smart home strategy under new CEO John Ternus, beginning with the launch of a long-delayed home hub on October 13. Further connected-home devices are expected to follow.

title: French Firm Mistral Is Hiring in Canada as It Expands Its Sovereign AI Business
summary: Mistral AI, which has already signed a deal with the Quebec government, is recruiting technical and sales staff in Canada to meet business demand. The expansion positions the French company to compete for Canadian sovereign AI contracts.
